questions.question: You ran this mostly alone with full access to everything — what changes if a team of engineers, not one person, tries to run these lanes and gates?
questions.why: The whole method rests on one person setting gates, reviewing, and flipping production, which raises adoption doubts for a team.

questions.question: What was the total cost of this project, including the Claude Max subscription itself, not just the nine dollars of metered spend?
questions.why: The cost line only calls out the small metered spend and buries the subscription cost, which a budget owner would want in full.

questions.question: Who sets the pass/fail bar for each gate, and how do you stop that number from being picked to guarantee the result you want?
questions.why: The favorite-idea bar of losing two points was set by the speaker himself before testing it, which looks like it could be gamed.

questions.question: Is about two in three on live auctions good enough to ship, and what's the next number you're actually trying to move?
questions.why: The speaker calls the result 'not done, but measurable' without saying what threshold would count as shippable.

questions.question: When a gate passes and code merges, who actually decides to flip it to production, and is there any check before that happens?
questions.why: The gates-and-flags method leaves production flips as a manual call by one person with no described review step.

questions.question: For a product manager who isn't writing code or running worktrees, what's the concrete first thing to do differently on Monday?
questions.why: The closing slide's next steps are written for someone who can set up worktrees and flags, not for a non-technical role.

questions.question: The starter kit covers finding the fix, testing the idea, and checking it's done — why is there nothing repeatable for deciding what to build first?
questions.why: The cheat sheet leaves problem D as 'a conversation for your next planning meeting' instead of a process like the other three.

questions.question: A usage limit cut off three build lanes mid-work at one point — how would you plan capacity or budget around that at team scale?
questions.why: The speaker mentions a usage cap breaking mid-run as an aside without addressing what it means for reliability at scale.

questions.question: The persona panel said done and your own phone said otherwise the next morning — has that gap shown up again since you added the live-browser step?
questions.why: The fix for the panel's blind spot is recent, so it's worth asking whether it has actually held up since.

questions.question: About how many of the roughly hundred experiments ran fully unattended overnight versus needing you to check in or intervene?
questions.why: The talk claims cheap unattended experimentation but doesn't break down how much of it truly needed no babysitting.
